physics_goals.quote: was operated from 2003 until 2010 in the Modane Underground Laboratory (LSM) to measure two-neutrino double β (2νββ) decays of seven isotopes in the form of thin foils and to search for
physics_goals.value: Search for neutrinoless double beta decay, mainly of 100Mo, and measurement of two-neutrino double beta decay in seven isotopes

summary.plain: A cylindrical detector in the Modane laboratory, under the Frejus mountain, that followed the two electrons of double beta decay track by track. From 2003 to 2010 it studied seven isotopes, mainly molybdenum-100, and found no neutrinoless decay.
summary.technical: NEMO-3: thin source foils (100Mo 6.914 kg, 82Se 0.932 kg, 116Cd 0.405 kg and others, about 20 m2) between a Geiger-cell tracking chamber (6180 cells) and a plastic-scintillator calorimeter, in a 25 G solenoid field with iron and water shielding; electron/positron separation by curvature. Final 100Mo result with 34.3 kg y: T1/2(0vbb) > 1.1e24 yr (90 % C.L.).
